title: Australia PR Points 2026: Skilled Migration Points Test Guide
metaDescription: Australia PR points test 2026: minimum 65 points to lodge an EOI, age, English, experience and qualification points, and why most invites need 85+ points.
headline: Australia PR Points 2026: Complete Points Test Guide

sections.title: How the Australia PR Points Test Works
sections.content:
Australia's General Skilled Migration programme uses a points test for the Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189), the Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) and the Skilled Work Regional visa (subclass 491). You need at least 65 points to submit an Expression of Interest through SkillSelect, but 65 points only makes you eligible, it does not guarantee an invitation.

Before points even count, you need an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list and a positive skills assessment from the assessing authority for that occupation, such as Engineers Australia, ACS or VETASSESS. You must also be under 45 at the time of invitation and hold at least Competent English.

sections.title: Where Points Come From
sections.content:
Age gives the biggest single block: 30 points for ages 25 to under 33, 25 points for 18 to under 25 and 33 to under 40, and 15 points for 40 to under 45. English adds 10 points for Proficient level and 20 points for Superior level, while a bachelor's or master's degree adds 15 points.

Skilled employment adds up to 15 points for overseas experience and 20 points for Australian experience, and extras include 5 points for state nomination under subclass 190, 15 points for regional nomination under subclass 491, and up to 10 points for a skilled partner. A government review of the points test has been announced, but no new values had been published as of October 2026.

sections.title: How Many Points Actually Get Invited
sections.content:
In 2026 invitation rounds, most professional occupations needed 80 points or more, and competitive applicants scored 85 to 95 points or higher, while some construction trades were invited at 65 points. Nurses were reported around 70 to 75 points and teachers around 80 to 90 points in recent rounds.

If your score sits near 65 to 75 points, the realistic options are state nomination through subclass 190, regional nomination through subclass 491, employer sponsorship, or building points first through better English scores, more skilled experience or partner points.

faqs.q: What is the minimum points score for Australia PR in 2026?
faqs.a: The legal minimum is 65 points on the skilled migration points test to lodge an Expression of Interest for subclass 189, 190 or 491. However, 65 points only buys eligibility, not an invitation, and most professional occupations in 2026 rounds required 80 points or more, so applicants should treat 65 as a floor rather than a target.

faqs.q: How are age points calculated for Australia PR?
faqs.a: Age points are assessed at the time of invitation: 25 points for ages 18 to under 25, 30 points for 25 to under 33, 25 points for 33 to under 40 and 15 points for 40 to under 45. Applicants must be under 45 when invited, so timing matters: points drop at 33 and again at 40.

faqs.q: How many points does English give in the Australia points test?
faqs.a: Competent English, such as IELTS 6.0 in each component, is the minimum requirement and gives zero points, while Proficient English at IELTS 7.0 gives 10 points and Superior English at IELTS 8.0 gives 20 points. PTE Academic is also accepted, and moving from Proficient to Superior English is often the fastest way to add 10 points.

faqs.q: Can state nomination help if my Australia PR points are low?
faqs.a: Yes, state or territory nomination under subclass 190 adds 5 points and leads to permanent residence, while regional nomination under subclass 491 adds 15 points but grants a provisional visa. Both routes can turn a 65 to 75 point profile into a competitive one, although each state sets its own occupation lists and nomination criteria.
